'akhti' at 57:26 = engine for ta5ti (her chat). عمان at 00:33 is a name. rows.chat: EL-YOAM Benet 3ammi badat/ballashat teshte8el fi ma7alli u kaan laazem a3allemha kulshi
rows.why: He used ta3allam (learn) / 3amal (do) in the past for 'teach her'; Amal recast with a3allemha (causative 3allem, bare present after laazem).

rows.chat: heye z8eere kteer u ma ba3ref keef heyye ra7 teshte8el
rows.why: He stalled on the word for 'young'; Amal prompted صـ... then supplied صغيرة (his words not transcribed).

rows.medi_said: make her a good [speaking Arabic] ... If I say [speaking Arabic], it wouldn't make sense?
rows.amal_said: أنا لازم تصير؟ No. You'd need something like to make her، to make to let her become. ... أخليها تصير
rows.chat: bas ana ra7 ajrreb a5alliha t9eer muwazzafe mnee7a
rows.why: Amal echoed his 'ana laazem t9eer' and said No - 'make/let her become' needs a5alli + pronoun + bare verb.
rows.english: I'm going to try to make her a good employee
rows.proposed_rule: To say 'make / let someone become X' use a5alli + object ending + bare verb: a5alliha t9eer muwazzafe mnee7a.

rows.chat: bas ana ra7 ajrreb a5alliha t9eer muwazzafe mnee7a
rows.why: He reached for 'employee' and Amal supplied موظفة (sheet: employee | Muwazzaf).

rows.medi_said: بسوار وبنـ... ... بنسـ-- بنسوار أو بسوار؟
rows.amal_said: No، بصور، but صور. ... the only one that was an was بكسر، بانكسر.
rows.why: Recalling verb pairs he built an n- partner for basawwer; Amal said No - only بكسر/بنكسر takes n-, the pair is with t- (he then: 'It was a T not an N'). Partly a question.

rows.amal_said: What excites you؟ One thing. ... No، it's present، بس it's one، not group of things. ... شو بيحمسك؟
rows.why: He put the plural 'they' -u on the verb for 'what excites you'; Amal: 'No... it's one, not group of things' and gave شو بيحمسك.

rows.amal_said: Made. ... Past. He made me excited.
rows.why: He used the present for 'he made me excited'; Amal prompted 'Made... Past' and he fixed to hamasni.

rows.amal_said: Mm. Get excited, not excite me or someone. ... It's the wrong verb. It's get excited, not excite.
rows.why: For the command 'get excited' he used 7ammes (excite someone); Amal named it the wrong verb - it needs the t- form.
He put an extra te- prefix on the command; Amal: 'No T, just one T' -> t7ammasi.

rows.amal_said: This is why don't you get excited? ... we are using the adjective here because it's are.
rows.why: He used a negated verb for 'why aren't you excited (now)'; Amal explained it needs the adjective mit7ammse with mish.
'We got excited' needs the t- form t7ammasna (her chat); he said 7ammasna (we excited [someone]) and she let it pass - engine may have dropped the t.

rows.medi_said: fi el shara. Or ala el shara? No, fi el shara.
rows.amal_said: street. What's the road? ... Like the way on the road.
rows.why: He used شارع (street) for 'road'; Amal: 'street. What's the road?' and he changed to ala el taree- (sheet: on the road / way | 3ala el-6aree2).

rows.amal_said: الـ safar. Safra is one trip. Safar is...
rows.why: He used safra (one trip) for 'travelling'; Amal recast to el-safar and explained the difference.
He left the -ni 'me' ending off the command; Amal prompted 'Me. Excite me.' and he fixed to hamasini.

rows.medi_said: They got too excited. Humma ziyada.
rows.amal_said: Let's put it at the after.
rows.why: He put ziyada straight after humma; Amal told him to put it after (the verb) and he built ta hamasu ziyada.
He used kaan (he was) for 'I was'; Amal recast قُنت and he repeated kunnet.

rows.medi_said: Ana kunnet ashtagil bi il AI
rows.why: Her chat has fi el-AI where he said bi il; she said nothing aloud.
'You (f)' after a vowel is -ki; he said afarjik / afarjinek and Amal recast أفرجيكي, which he repeated.

rows.chat: lamma ana biddi ba9eer a7san bi ishi laazem atmarran lamma 3indi wa2et
rows.why: Her chat of his sentence keeps b- after biddi (biddi ba9eer); after biddi the verb drops b-. Not voiced; transcript has no Arabic here.
rows.english: When I want to get better at something I have to practise when I have time

rows.why: رجل is feminine so the verb takes t-; Amal said 'is feminine' and he fixed to رجله بتوجع.

rows.medi_said: مرات أنا بيوجع, بيوجعك, uh, either بالغلط or, uh, مش قصدي. Eh, مش بقصد.
rows.why: With أنا the verb needs the I-form ba- (her chat bawajj3ek); he said beywajj3ek (he hurts you) and she moved on.
rows.english: Sometimes I hurt you by accident

rows.why: Sheet: 'intentionally / on purpose | Bel2asd | بالقصد'; he left out el-, she let it pass.

rows.amal_said: is did I hurt you? Did you get hurt?
rows.why: For 'did you get hurt' he put an object ending on the verb (sounds like 'did I hurt you'); Amal said so and he fixed to twajja3ti ('there wouldn't be a preposition').

rows.amal_said: No, by me. Because of me.
rows.why: 'Hurt by me' needs min + ending, not an object ending on the t- verb; Amal: 'No, by me' and he built توجعتي مني.
rows.english: Did you get hurt by me?

rows.why: He used the t- form (get hurt) for 'don't hurt her'; Amal repeated the prompt and he reached ma twajj3iha.
A negative command is ma + the you-form; he dropped the t- prefix, Amal said 'Very close' and he fixed to ma tiwajaiha.
7aka takes la- (her chat 7akkaitili); he put a direct object -ni on it and she let it pass.
rows.english: I got hurt by what you told me

rows.medi_said: daya u-- daya u ni. Daya u ni.
rows.why: He put 'me' (-ni) for 'you'; Amal prompted 'You.' and he fixed to daya u ki.
After illi the verb points back with -h (her chat 3meltih); Amal said عملت once but he kept amalti and she later said ممتاز, so read as let pass.

rows.amal_said: بي. ... كان بيضايق not ت 'cause it makes people upset. It upsets.
rows.why: 'Was upsetting' needs daaye2 (upsets others), not the t- form etdaaya2 (get upset); Amal named it. (Her b- after kaan is B7, not scored.)
For 'they' he said huwe; Amal said 'They.' and he switched to hume.
rows.english: I suppose they got upset with us

rows.why: He used bil3aks (on the contrary) for the noun 'opposite'; Amal recast ما عنده عكس and explained 3aks is the noun (sheet: opposite (bel-3aks = on the contrary) | 3aks).
Moving a thing to a side takes la-; Amal recast La el yameen and explained 3ala is for giving directions.
rows.english: I moved my bed to the right

rows.why: Her chat has lal-shmaal (la + el-); he used fus7a ila with no el- and she let it pass.

rows.amal_said: Ashya ak or ashya ek. Ashya e.
rows.why: He asked how to make 'your things'; Amal supplied the plural ashyaa2ek - a didn't-know.

rows.medi_said: Um, [speaking Arabic] ... [speaking Arabic] Two is ala?
rows.amal_said: هذي الطاولة. And it's لوين. ... We added to the question to always. ... From to is la.
rows.why: 'Where to' must carry la- in front (lawain); Amal named it and he repeated lawain ('I don't think I've ever said this before').
rows.english: Where will you move this table to?

rows.why: Amal recast 'this table' as هذي الطاولة right after his untranscribed try; what he said is not visible.

rows.why: For 'the papers' he used ورقة (one sheet); Amal explained ورق is the plural.
rows.english: The papers moved from the wind
